title: Predicting LLM Inference Latency: A Roofline-Driven ML Method
summary_zh: 提出一個融合解析 Roofline 模型 (RLM) 與學習式迴歸器的 LLM 推理延遲預測方法。核心觀察：純 Roofline 解析估計因假設硬體全程運行於額定時脈與峰值頻寬而系統性高估效能，作者將此落差歸因於「雲端基礎設施與動態工作負載引入的變異性」，並以 RF／XGB／LR 迴歸器吸收殘差——將 RLM 估計作為附加特徵。在 vLLM 與 Triton、單張 A100 上以四個 Hugging Face 模型 (opt-1.3b、phi-2、pythia-1.4b、gpt2-xl) 驗證：納入 RLM 特徵使 vLLM 平均 R² 提升 12.93%、MSE 下降 80.08%（opt-1.3b 達 R²+17 點、MSE−87%）；Triton 提升 R² 4.25%、MSE 下降 61.98%。平均計算受限比例超過 19.5%，證明方法不限於記憶體受限運算。與我們最相近的先前工作：他們看見我們的殘差卻將其誤標為雲端雜訊，從未指認 GPU SM 時脈下垂這一機制。
summary_en: Proposes an LLM inference-latency predictor that fuses an analytical Roofline Model (RLM) with a learned regressor. Core observation: the pure Roofline analytical estimate systematically over-predicts performance because it assumes the hardware sustains its rated clock and peak bandwidth throughout; the authors attribute this gap to "variability introduced by cloud infrastructure and dynamic workloads" and absorb the residual with RF/XGB/LR regressors that take the RLM estimate as an extra feature. Validated on vLLM and Triton with a single A100 across four Hugging Face models (opt-1.3b, phi-2, pythia-1.4b, gpt2-xl): adding the RLM feature raises average R² by 12.93% and cuts MSE by 80.08% on vLLM (opt-1.3b alone gains +17 R² points and −87% MSE), and improves Triton R² by 4.25% with a 61.98% MSE reduction. The average compute-bound ratio exceeds 19.5%, showing the method is not limited to memory-bound operations. The closest prior art to ours: they see our residual but mislabel it as cloud noise, never identifying the GPU SM clock-droop mechanism.
